PullRequest.Title: Fix Markdown pull diagnostics for rich-editor-only tabs
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #342138

## Summary
Upgrade `vscode-languageclient` from 8.0.2 to 9.0.1 so built-in Markdown pull diagnostics include custom-editor tabs. Documents opened only in the rich editor now receive diagnostics without a companion text-editor tab.

- Use 9.0.1 because it already contains custom-tab tracking and preserves the existing desktop/browser and module-resolution contracts; no unrelated 10.x migration is needed.
- Keep the existing diagnostic collection/renderer integration and language-server version unchanged.
- Add an integration regression verifying a broken fragment link produces a warning and correcting it clears diagnostics, while asserting no text-editor tab or visible text editor exists for the document.
- Document the diagnostic architecture and validation expectations.

## Validation
- 44 focused integration tests passed, including rich-only pull diagnostics, diagnostics/completion, rename, Markdown rendering/front matter, and document-link handling.
- Confirmed the regression fails with 8.0.2: it times out waiting for diagnostics with an empty collection.
- Desktop TypeScript emit, browser typecheck, desktop/browser bundles, and regression-test lint passed.
- Validation ran in a disposable export with an isolated Code OSS test instance; no dependencies were installed or tests run in the worktree, and the running development checkout was left untouched.

Scenarios.Scenario: Desktop and browser Markdown extension activation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Extension activation awaits LanguageClient.start(), including creation and initialization of the existing desktop language-server process or browser worker, before shared Markdown features are registered.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Starts the Markdown language-server module with IPC transport.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One process per desktop extension activation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Version 8.0.2 used the same LanguageClient construction, server module, IPC transport, and awaited start.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Creates one browser Worker for the Markdown language server and posts localization initialization data.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One worker per browser extension activation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same worker creation and client startup path existed before the dependency upgrade.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The worker-backed client is started before activation completes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One activation per extension-host lifetime; independent of the number of custom-editor tabs at activation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single Markdown language server is created per activated extension instance; no changed loop or burst scheduler is present in repository code.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The server/client remain warm for the extension lifetime. The dependency upgrade changes implementation code but introduces no repository-visible cache key, miss path, or invalidation change.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that startup retains the same process/worker cardinality and call path; low evidence of any changed expensive startup mechanism.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The bundled byte-size and initialization-cost delta of vscode-languageclient 9.0.1 is not available in the supplied repository sources, so no startup regression can be established from the version number or lockfile alone.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the diff changes dependency versions but does not prove added startup boundaries, repeated initialization, or increased concurrency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open and edit a Markdown document only in the rich custom editor with validation enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening the editor is not shown to await diagnostics. The upgraded language client now recognizes the custom-editor tab and asynchronously pulls diagnostics from the already-running server; edits use the pre-existing onChange pull option. Diagnostic collection changes notify the rich-editor webview, which requests and maps current diagnostics.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Sends pull-diagnostic requests between the extension-side language client and the existing Markdown language server for custom-editor-only resources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At least one pull for an opened qualifying custom-only resource and subsequent changed-resource pulls when validation is active; no evidence that each tab event re-pulls every tab.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: With vscode-languageclient 8.0.2, custom-editor-only tabs were not tracked for pulls, so this resource produced no diagnostic request until represented by a text-editor tab.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Diagnostic availability depends on the round trip, but editor opening/rendering is not shown to block on it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: When opt-in file-link validation is enabled, the server checks linked target files; local fragment validation parses the current document without this boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Potentially proportional to distinct file-link targets in each newly validated custom-only document; exact server caching/deduplication is not available in supplied sources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same validation existed for text-editor-backed resources, but custom-editor-only resources did not reach it before this upgrade.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs behind asynchronous diagnostic pulls and delays diagnostic publication, not rich-editor opening.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Notifies each live rich-editor webview that diagnostics changed; the webview can request mapped diagnostics from the extension host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One notification per matching diagnostics event per live panel for that document; multiple editors per document can fan out, but this listener and fan-out predate the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The webview bridge already existed, but no server diagnostic-change event was produced for a custom-editor-only resource under the old client.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Updates decorations asynchronously after diagnostics arrive.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective work scales with affected open custom-only Markdown resources and their edit events; server validation also scales with document/link count, while webview mapping scales with the diagnostics returned for that document.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Requests share the single Markdown language server. The dependency's internal pull scheduler is not present in repository sources, but the diff and test establish per-resource custom-tab reachability, not an unbounded workspace-wide launch or explicit Promise.all burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The client tracks tab/resource state for the extension lifetime and pull diagnostics may use protocol result state, but implementation details are outside the supplied source. Closing the custom tab is exercised by the test, and existing editor listeners are disposed on panel disposal. Validation defaults to disabled, so costly link validation is opt-in.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the newly reachable per-resource diagnostic IPC and downstream webview update; insufficient evidence that the implementation amplifies this into repeated all-tab work, uncontrolled concurrency, or retained state.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The dependency's exact tab-event coalescing and diagnostic result-cache implementation is unavailable, and no benchmark quantifies validation cost for very large link-heavy documents.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the added boundary is the intended opt-in diagnostic feature, is off the editor-open critical path, defaults to disabled, and the diff provides no evidence of redundant workspace-wide fan-out or an unbounded lifecycle.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The test writes one temporary file, updates two workspace settings, opens one custom editor, polls the in-process diagnostics collection until two conditions are met, then closes the tab, deletes the file, and restores settings.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Creates and later deletes one temporary Markdown file, saving it first if dirty.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One create and one delete per test run.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This integration test and its temporary file operations did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both setup and cleanup await the filesystem operations.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Opens one custom editor and waits for the language-client/server diagnostic round trips triggered by opening and editing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One opened resource and two expected diagnostic states per test run.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No equivalent rich-only diagnostics regression test existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The test waits up to ten seconds for each state; this affects test duration only.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant one file and one tab; polling is bounded to 200 reads over ten seconds per wait.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Operations are awaited sequentially except asynchronous language-server diagnostics; no parallel test fan-out is introduced in this file.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The test intentionally uses a unique URI to avoid warm diagnostic state and restores workspace configuration in finally; no persistent cache is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that all added I/O and polling are test-only and bounded.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Runner parallelism outside this file is not shown, but this test's own resource use is constant and bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the bounded test work has no product runtime impact and does not create a meaningful CI scaling regression.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all four changed files and all diff pages. Traced activation, newly reachable custom-tab pull diagnostics, downstream webview updates, optional filesystem validation, lifecycle cleanup, and the integration test. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was established, so no findings were submitted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
